claims.statement: Inferential error and belief updating in preference processes are generally path-dependent under model misspecification.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that inference and belief updating decompose into path-dependent components under model misspecification.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

nodes.title: General Preference Oracles and Path Dependence in Preference Formation

detail.title: General Preference Oracles and Path Dependence in Preference Formation
detail.summary: Revised analysis incorporating path-dependent inferential errors under model misspecification into preference formation frameworks.
detail.findings: Inferential error and belief updating in preference processes are generally path-dependent under model misspecification. [source-0f17f7655d614a90]
detail.limitations: Empirical validation remains restricted to specific binary inference configurations and misspecified model regimes.
detail.next_questions: How do path-dependent components interact with multi-agent preference aggregation over longer horizons?
detail.reason: Revising notebook-proj-emergent-prefs-01-v1 with new evidence source-0f17f7655d614a90 to address path dependence in preference evolution.

review.alternative: Belief processes might converge to a path-independent equilibrium if strong correcting feedback loops are present.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration of complete path independence across diverse misspecified model initializations.

claims.statement: Inferential error and belief updating in preference processes are generally path-dependent under model misspecification.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that inference and belief updating decompose into path-dependent components under model misspecification.
support.passage: inferential error, of a given belief process vs another (e.g. true probability), is in general not path-independent (not round-tripping despite the given belief process doing so); it decomposes uniquely into twoindependentcompo- nents, one path-independent, systematic and identifiable as a well-known behavioural bias, one path-dependent and not necessarily systematic.

review.alternative: Belief processes might converge to a path-independent equilibrium if strong correcting feedback loops are present.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration of complete path independence across diverse misspecified model initializations.

support_provenance.statement: Inferential error and belief updating in preference processes are generally path-dependent under model misspecification.

detail.title: Epistemic Justice and Foundational Assumptions in AI Metareasoning
detail.summary: Integrating epistemic justice frameworks to understand how foundational assumptions are recognized and challenged in automated reasoning.
detail.findings: Epistemic justice and inclusion frameworks provide a structural basis for identifying and contesting foundational assumptions in complex systems. [source-01dc40b4486b4efe]
detail.limitations: Direct empirical demonstrations of autonomous self-correction remain limited across complex architectures.
detail.next_questions: How can community-grounded knowledge frameworks be systematically integrated into automated reasoning verification?
detail.reason: Revising the notebook to incorporate new source evidence concerning epistemic justice and foundational assumptions.
